name: 挑战模式
description: Quiz challenge + world boss, migrated out of api/modules/challenge (P4.3b). Adopts challenge_records and world_bosses under their legacy names; reads question_bank and the legacy pets table (both owned elsewhere) through declared read access; appends to the shared point ledger only through classroom.public.

data._adopted_note: Both tables are written only by this domain and keep their legacy names because `SELECT *` rows for world_bosses go straight through to the frontend (max_hp, start_time, ... are part of the HTTP contract). Renaming is the coordinated P7 namespace migration tracked by guardrail G10. NOTE: api/modules/classroom/classroom.service.ts still reads world_bosses directly for its dashboard - that legacy reader has to become a classroom-side concern or a port when classroom migrates.
data._reads_note: Neither table belongs to challenge, and neither has a port: `question_bank` is authored by the system domain (now plugins/system, P4.3b.5a) and cleaned up by admin, and `pets.attack_power` is the pet domain's legacy table - PetPort exposes no attack-power accessor, so the world-boss damage roll reads the one column directly. Both are read-only here; a write would be refused by the ownership check. The 500-on-fresh-database gap this note used to warn about is GONE: it was caused by `ensureAdoptedSchema` only creating `data.adopted` tables while the legacy `initDb()` DDL did not run in the kernel composition, and P4.3c.2 replaced both with one boot-schema migration that `api/app.ts` injects via `createKernel({ migrations: [bootSchemaMigration] })`. Probe-verified afterwards: `question_bank`, `pets` and `operation_logs` are all present on a fresh in-memory kernel-composition database and GET /api/challenge/questions answers 200 with an empty list. A boot that supplies no migrations at all still creates only the kernel tables - that is the intended kernel-only deployment, tracked by P4.3c.3.
